Pipeline Select a stage to see what happens when it fails

gRPC acks=all poll _bulk

An illustration of the delivery rules, not measured data.

agent

Does
Tails log files and gives each line an ID from its file position. Each batch is written to a disk spool with fsync before it’s sent.
If it fails
Spooled batches survive the crash. A batch is deleted only after the collector acks it, so anything unacknowledged is resent on restart.

collector

Does
gRPC server. Checks the API key, rejects invalid entries, and publishes to Kafka partitioned by service, waiting for all replicas to confirm.
If it fails
It acks the agent only after Kafka confirms the write. No ack means the agent keeps the batch and resends it with exponential backoff.

kafka

Does
Buffers records between ingestion and indexing, so a slow indexer doesn’t push back on the agents.
If it fails
The collector can’t get a confirmed write, so it never acks. Batches stay in the agents’ spools until Kafka is back.

indexer

Does
Kafka consumer group. Bulk-writes into daily indices and commits its offsets only after OpenSearch accepts the writes. Records it can’t parse go to a dead-letter topic.
If it fails
A crash between the write and the commit means Kafka redelivers those records. They carry the same IDs, so they overwrite the earlier copies.

opensearch

Does
Stores each line as a document keyed by its log ID. The query API on top supports filters by time, service, level, and text, with cursor pagination.
If it fails
The indexer retries failed items and holds off on committing, so the records wait in Kafka until OpenSearch recovers.
How it was tested

Each chaos scenario writes 60,000 lines at 3,000 lines/s, injects a fault four seconds in, heals it, and then runs the checker. All 17 passed with zero missing lines in three full runs, using the whole stack in Docker on one laptop.

Process kills
SIGKILL the collector, Kafka, the indexer, the agent, or OpenSearch.
Network faults
Toxiproxy cuts the links to the collector, Kafka, and OpenSearch, adds 800 ms of latency, resets connections, throttles Kafka to 50 KB/s, and blackholes OpenSearch.
Forced duplicates
Drop the collector’s acks, or kill the indexer after a write but before its offset commit. These fail unless OpenSearch absorbs the redundant writes.
Crash loops
Kill the collector and the indexer three times each, and kill every service in sequence.

The throughput limit is the indexer’s poll, write, commit cycle, not the agents or the collector.
